races.title: State Assembly, District 68
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jessie Lopez
cands.bio: Santa Ana City Council member for Ward 3 since December 2020. Born and raised in Santa Ana. Studied at Santa Ana College and CSU Long Beach. Says she worked in law firms before taking office. Democratic candidate for State Assembly District 68 in 2026.

endorsements.text: U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, Working Families Party, California Nurses Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund (as listed by Ballotpedia).
Congressman Derek Tran, Sen. Caroline Menjivar, Assemblymember Alex Lee, OC Supervisor Vicente Sarmiento, and Dolores Huerta (as listed on her campaign site).

cands.gaps: We found no independent news coverage of her time on the Santa Ana City Council, so her council actions on rezonings, development, data centers or property taxes are not documented here. Claims about her rent-cap, eviction-protection and lobbyist-transparency work come only from her own survey and campaign site. Her campaign site links to stories about a former landlord's lawsuit and a "600% raise" claim tied to Measure FF. We saw only the headlines and teasers, which are the campaign's own framing, so we left them out. The reasons for the 2023 recall are not in the pages we have. We could not confirm which law firms she worked for or in what roles. We found nothing on her positions on homestead property taxes, abortion restrictions, gun laws, school vouchers or charters, teacher pay, or H-1B visas.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Santa Ana, and her own 2024 survey and her campaign site both say she was born and raised in Santa Ana.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Santa Ana City Council member (Ward 3) since December 2020, re-elected in 2024 and survived a 2023 recall election. She says she worked in corporate law firms before holding office and that she has delivered the city's budget each year.
qual.why: Local elected office of about five years, including city budget work, puts her in the middle band. She has no state legislative service. Her law-firm work is self-described and her specific roles are not documented.
qual.label: Local elected office of about five years, including city budget work, puts her in the middle band. She has no state legislative service. Her law-firm work is self-described and her specific roles are not documented.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Her campaign site lists a priority to "Keep Data Centers Out of the Region," citing protecting the environment and conserving resources.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says to "End Flock Cameras in AD-68" over mass-surveillance and privacy concerns. This covers only the Flock camera part of the plank; the site says nothing about gun laws.

land-for-floridians.evidence: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she said she will fight to "stop corporations from buying single family homes."

workers-first.evidence: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she wrote "Abolish ICE!" and said she is committed to policies that keep families together. Her campaign site lists protecting immigrant communities from ICE as a priority.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In her 2020 Ballotpedia survey she said she would keep fighting to protect public lands and green space, and she volunteered with the Rise Up Willowick coalition for community-driven development and environmental justice.

clean-money.evidence: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she said she is "not backed by corporate interests" and does not answer to them. In 2020 she wrote that politicians should represent residents, "not their donors." These are statements, not a formal pledge to refuse any category of contribution.

prio.label: Matches 5 of 6 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 5 only promised

roots.summary: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Santa Ana, and her own 2024 survey and her campaign site both say she was born and raised in Santa Ana.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site priority: "Keep Data Centers Out of the Region. Protect our environment, conserve our resources, and say no to draining our communities."

cands.name: David Penaloza
cands.bio: Santa Ana City Council member (Ward 6) and Mayor Pro Tem, first elected in 2018. Senior Regulatory Manager at Color Science, Inc. Elected President of the Orange County Division of the League of California Cities in 2025. Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 68 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, California Young Democrats, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund.

In his own survey he also lists CAYIMBY, California Professional Firefighters, LA/OC Building Trades, LIUNA, the Latino Legislative Caucus, AFSCME California, Assembly Speaker Robert Rivas and Assemblymember Avelino Valencia. These are his own claims.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or whether he lived elsewhere at any point. We found no stated position on data centers, property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His council voting record was not in the sources, so we can't show specific actions on these issues. The Police Oversight Commission claim comes only from his own survey and has not been checked against city records.

local.label: Roots 90: In his Ballotpedia survey he calls himself a lifelong Santa Ana resident raised in the Memorial Park neighborhood and educated in Santa Ana Unified schools, but no birthplace is given.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Santa Ana City Council member since first winning election in 2018, now Mayor Pro Tem. Also a Senior Regulatory Manager at Color Science, Inc., and has been President of the Orange County Division of the League of California Cities. No state legislative service found.
qual.why: Local elected office and a management career fit the middle band. There is no prior state legislative service or direct budget or law career in the sources.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Said in his Ballotpedia survey that he supports expanding housing and homeownership by streamlining responsible development and reducing unnecessary barriers to construction.

back-police-order.evidence: Said in his Ballotpedia survey that he has supported public safety investments on the City Council and wants to address quality-of-life crimes and reckless street takeovers. He also said he brought forward a Police Oversight Commission.
